source.title: Generalization Through The Lens Of Leave-One-Out Error
source.authors: Gregor Bachmann; Thomas Hofmann; Aurélien Lucchi

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates random-label generalization behavior using NTK and random-feature kernel models, reporting train, test, and leave-one-out behavior; this is a kernel-based conceptual test rather than the original finite-network SGD experiment.
record.gate_note: Section 4.2 reports cited prior-work statements about small empirical error on random labels, which are not rows. The paper's own random-label results are test and LOO error/accuracy, not training error; its random-feature appendix also reports test guessing and a loss spike. No values used only in figures are transcribed.
record.test_reason: Section 4.2 varies label corruption and measures clean-label test performance in an infinitely wide NTK model, bearing on V4. It assumes a full-rank kernel, which guarantees interpolation analytically; it does not test finite-network SGD fitting or optimization time.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the label-noise experiments. More broadly, the authors conclude that LOO captures generalization in kernel-regime models, prove an interpolation-threshold loss spike, and demonstrate accurate transfer-performance estimation.
record.recipe_differences: Kernel/NTK models and closed-form leave-one-out evaluation; random-feature model used for the fully randomized-label appendix result. The paper does not reproduce the original finite-network SGD training experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset (MNIST versus CIFAR10) and model formulation (NTK versus random features) vary; the random-feature fully randomized-label appendix uses binary MNIST with n = 2000, while the NTK label-noise experiment uses n = 20000.

fits_no_version.finding: Clean-label LOO loss and accuracy closely match corresponding test quantities under label corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LOO estimates generalization performance accurately in the tested NTK label-noise settings.

fits_no_version.finding: A random-feature model guesses randomly with fully randomized labels across widths, while test and LOO losses spike near interpolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Chance-level classification accuracy can coexist with an interpolation-associated squared-loss spike.

record.problems: For the label-noise experiment, numerical values are shown only in plots; the text provides qualitative trends. The paper does not report training error for its random-label experiments, so perfect fitting cannot be assessed from its own results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result rows identified. Figure-only values were not estimated from plots.

untested.parts: Random-label training error and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters for standard deep networks trained with stochastic gradient methods.
Training-time ratios and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Empirical verification of perfect training fit throughout the noise sweep; interpolation follows from the section's full-rank, unregularized kernel setup instead.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
The temporal order of learning real patterns and memorizing noise.

record.verdict_notes: No directional V4 verdict is justified from the supplied text alone: the worsening-with-noise statement is attributed to prior studies, and the current experiment's curves are unavailable in the text rendering. Figure-only values were already declared unextracted. Full-rank interpolation is a mathematical property of the setup, not a reported SGD training result.

versions.untested_parts: The paper studies random labels in kernel/NTK settings, but does not report its own training-error result or whether random labeling reaches zero training error under unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
It reports test and leave-one-out degradation over label-noise levels, but does not report its own training error across those levels or establish that training fit remains perfect.

rows.subject: 5-layer fully-connected NTK model
rows.operation_detail: Train on labels with a subset randomized at noise level p; evaluate against clean labels.
rows.measure: Test loss and accuracy as a function of label noise
rows.value: Test loss and accuracy worsen with increasing p; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The text describes an increasing-noise sweep and says test and LOO results almost perfectly match; numerical plot values are not stated.
rows.check: The supplied Figure 2 contains no readable curves or values. The study's own prose establishes agreement between test and LOO quantities, but does not explicitly establish the extracted worsening trend. Increasing loss and decreasing accuracy should also be distinguished.

rows.subject: 5-layer fully-connected NTK model
rows.operation_detail: Train on labels with a subset randomized at noise level p; evaluate leave-one-out error against clean labels.
rows.measure: LOO loss and accuracy as a function of label noise, evaluated against clean labels
rows.value: LOO loss and accuracy closely match the test quantities across settings; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: LOO is constructed to evaluate against the true clean labels rather than the randomized training labels.
rows.check: Agreement of clean-label LOO estimates with test results measures the proposed estimator's performance; agreement alone does not establish V4's degradation trend or perfect training fit.

rows.subject: random feature model
rows.operation_detail: Fit random labels on binary MNIST while varying feature width; report test and LOO behavior.
rows.value: The model randomly guesses throughout all overparameterization regimes.
rows.note: This is not a report of training error; it bears on test-at-chance behavior only.
rows.check: Random guessing is explicitly reported, but this frozen-feature model's test accuracy alone cannot establish random-label fitting by standard deep networks trained with stochastic gradient methods.

rows.subject: random feature model
rows.operation_detail: Fit random labels on binary MNIST while varying feature width; report test and LOO behavior.
rows.measure: Test and LOO loss across width
rows.value: Both exhibit a strong spike around the interpolation threshold; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The result concerns a double-descent loss spike and does not report training error.
rows.check: The reported loss spike concerns double descent across feature widths, rather than any version's fitting, corruption-fraction trend, or learning-time behavior.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: 5-layer fully-connected NTK models on MNIST and CIFAR10, n = 20000
reader_labels.reason: Test and clean-label LOO error worsen as noise increases, and the paper reports an almost perfect match between them (R1–R4). This supports the test-error trend, while the training-fit part is untested.
